root_cause.text: In net/sched sch_qfq, qfq_change_class() used a shared error path that unconditionally freed `cl->qdisc` and `cl` even when `cl` referred to an already existing class being modified, causing use-after-free of the live class object.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the `destroy_class:` path from unconditional `qdisc_put(cl->qdisc); kfree(cl);` to `if (!existing) { ... }`, and the commit message explicitly says “do not free existing class in qfq_change_class()” and warns that `cl->qdisc and cl should only be freed if a new class and qdisc were allocated, or we risk various UAF.`

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid freeing existing classes in qfq_change_class error handling while still cleaning up newly created ones.
intent_record.what: The cleanup code in the destroy_class error path was changed from always calling qdisc_put(cl->qdisc) and kfree(cl) to doing those operations only when !existing, by wrapping both calls in an if (!existing) conditional.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents the function from releasing the qdisc and freeing the class object when the error path is handling an already existing class, avoiding accidental destruction of existing state and potential use-after-free or double-free behavior; newly created classes are still cleaned up on error.

grouping_result.intent: Avoid freeing existing classes in qfq_change_class error handling while still cleaning up newly created ones.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by distinguishing newly created classes from existing ones in qfq_change_class error handling, preventing unconditional freeing of a live existing class and its qdisc.

candidates.rationale: This unconditional cleanup on the shared error path releases the qdisc of cl even when cl is an existing class being modified rather than a newly allocated class, directly causing use-after-free of a live object.
This unconditional free on the shared error path deallocates cl even when it points to an already existing class, which is the core bug leading to use-after-free of the live class object.

vuln_statements.explanation: This shared error-path statement unconditionally frees `cl` even when `cl` is an existing class being modified, directly causing the live class object to be freed and later used, which matches the root cause.

This shared error-path statement unconditionally drops the qdisc reference for `cl` even when `cl` refers to an already existing class, incorrectly tearing down state of a live object as part of the same faulty cleanup path.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet includes the full body of `qfq_change_class()` and its error handling, which is sufficient to assess the described root cause. The vulnerable construct is present because the function uses a shared error path `destroy_class:` that unconditionally executes `qdisc_destroy(cl->qdisc); kfree(cl);` at the end of `qfq_change_class()`. In this commit, `cl` may refer either to a newly allocated class or to an already existing class being modified: `struct qfq_class *cl = (struct qfq_class *)*arg;` and later `if (cl != NULL) { /* modify existing class */ ... existing = true; goto set_change_agg; }`. In the `set_change_agg:` path, if allocation of `new_agg` fails (`new_agg = kzalloc(sizeof(*new_agg), GFP_KERNEL); if (new_agg == NULL) { err = -ENOBUFS; gen_kill_estimator(&cl->bstats, &cl->rate_est); goto destroy_class; }`), execution jumps to `destroy_class:` even when `existing` is true and `cl` is a live pre-existing class. That path then destroys `cl->qdisc` and frees `cl`, which matches the root cause: freeing an existing class object during modification. The fix is not present because there is no conditional cleanup separating newly created classes from existing ones; the shared `destroy_class:` label still frees `cl` unconditionally.
